ai.description: The VUB Night Frog is a small amphibian (20–25 mm) with a mottled brown and grey body. It is distinguished by a pointed snout and prominent, fleshy webbing between its toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus vrijeuni* is best distinguished by its unique, significantly elongated third finger, which is proportionally longer than in other sympatric night frog species.
ai.habitat: *Nyctibatrachus vrijeuni* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations above 1,500m.
ai.behavior: The VUB Night Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden in leaf litter or rocky crevices during the day and emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus vrijeuni* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in rock crevices, which undergo direct development without a tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus vrijeuni* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically inhabiting high-elevation streams above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The VUB Night Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "ticking" notes, typically heard from vegetation near fast-flowing streams in its rainforest habitat.
